newsitem.title: GERMANY: Compaq targets doubling sales by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Compaq targets doubling sales by 2000.

text.p: U.S. computer group Compaq Computer Corp is targeting a doubling of sales to around $40 billion by the year 2000, Eckhard Pfeiffer, Compaq's chief executive officer, said on Tuesday.
"Both my management and myself believe we have a realistic chance of meeting this target," Pfeiffer said at an event in Munich.
This would involve annual turnover growth of 25 percent and would secure a position for Compaq among the top three computer groups in the world, he said.

The group said it hoped to reach this target by bringing in more networked technology, by introducing creative measures at all levels of the group's structure, by developing industrial partnerships and by investing in its employees.
Pfeiffer said Compaq had been the world's largest single producer of PCs since 1994, with a global market share of around ten percent.
Compaq said last week that its net income for the first quarter of 1997 rose to $387 million, or $1.36 a share, from $234 million, or 85 cents a share, a year earlier.
Worldwide sales grew 14.3 percent to $4.8 billion in the first quarter of 1997 from $4.2 billion the previous year.
